subject: Transitioning from Pay-as-you-go to Staged Prepay — reconciliation & top-up options
messages:
From: Susan Liu <susan.liu@orbitfs.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@orbitfs.com
Date: 2026-11-22T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Evaluating prepay options — ramp & auto top-ups

Hi Jordan,

We're looking at moving Orbit from PAYG to a committed prepay structure for model inference spend. Our goals: predictable unit pricing, smoothing month-to-month budget impact during our ramp, and a simple reconciliation process. Two quick questions to start: 1) can Redwood accommodate a staged prepay where credits are released monthly based on a ramp schedule, and 2) do you support threshold-triggered top-ups (auto top-up when remaining credits fall below X% with invoice/PO reconciliation)?

I've attached a very small usage export for the last 6 months to give you a sense of our profile. The procurement team is looped in on cc — Tom will own contract coordination.

Attachments: [Orbit_Usage_Profile_Nov2026.csv (CSV, 42KB)]

Thanks,
Susan Liu
Head of AI Platform
Orbit Financial Systems
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Susan Liu <susan.liu@orbitfs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-22T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Evaluating prepay options — ramp & auto top-ups

Hi Susan — thanks for the usage file, that's very helpful. Short answers: yes on staged release, and yes to threshold-triggered top-ups.

High-level approach I propose (summary):
- Staged credit releases: create a 12/24/36 month schedule where prepay funds are escrowed and released to Orbit's live ledger monthly per the ramp cadence (we can frontload or backload depending on discount profile).
- Threshold top-ups: configurable auto-topup at 15%/10% remaining threshold; top-ups can be charged to the PO or run as a monthly reconciliation invoice — your choice.
- Reconciliation: monthly lookback with a single debit/credit entry; unused credits at term-end can be either returned (refund) or applied as a final true-up per SOW.

I've sketched a worksheet and proposal for a 3-year and 12-month variant — attaching the draft. Could you confirm whether Orbit prefers: (A) predictably smoothed monthly release, or (B) heavier frontloaded credits in year 1 with step-downs after year 1? That will materially change the discount bands we can offer.

Next steps: if you like the sketch, Marissa will follow with pricing tiers and a draft SOW for legal/finance.

Attachment: [Redwood_Staged-TopUp-Proposal.xlsx (XLSX, 78KB)]

—
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Susan Liu <susan.liu@orbitfs.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@orbitfs.com>, procurement@orbitfs.com
Date: 2026-11-23T08:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Evaluating prepay options — ramp & auto top-ups

Jordan / Marissa,

Prefer option A — smoothed monthly release for predictability. For context: we expect rapid user onboarding in Q1 and Q2, so a predictable monthly credit release helps our FP&A forecast. Important constraints from procurement/finance: any auto top-up must be tied to a clear PO or be limited to a capped emergency pad (we can't have open indefinite charges). Also, we need auditability: per-token usage logs and per-route cost breakdowns for at least 12 months.

Tom — can you share the standard PO terms (net30) and any internal thresholds?

Thanks,
Susan
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Susan Liu <susan.liu@orbitfs.com>
Date: 2026-11-24T09:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Evaluating prepay options — ramp & auto top-ups

On Mon, Nov 23, 2026 at 08:42 AM Susan Liu <susan.liu@orbitfs.com> wrote:
> Jordan / Marissa,
>
> Prefer option A — smoothed monthly release for predictability. 

Susan — noted. From finance/legal perspective, a couple of operational controls we recommend for a smooth three-year prepay: 

1) Escrowed prepay with monthly ledger release: Redwood holds committed funds in a customer ledger; credits are released monthly per the agreed schedule.
2) Auto-topup guardrails: top-ups limited to (i) emergency pad of up to 10% of monthly committed credits (can be pre-authorized on PO) and (ii) manual approval for any charge that exceeds 150% of projected monthly run-rate.
3) End-of-term true-up options: unused credit refund (net of discounts) OR apply to final month(s) based on a pre-agreed rate.
4) Audit & logs: we can provide per-request logs (token counts, model id, route) retained for 13 months; access via our Console export + S3 link.

I'll draft contract language for: discount tapering if monthly release is fully consumed for 3 consecutive months (we'd re-evaluate discount bands), and a clause for PO-driven auto-topup that ties charges to a specific PO number.

Draft SOW/contract will be uploaded to DocuSign once we have agreement on the release cadence.

—
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Commercial Finance
Redwood Inference
Attachment: [SOW-Redwood-Orbit-v1.docx (DOCX, 92KB)]
From: Susan Liu <susan.liu@orbitfs.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@orbitfs.com>, procurement@orbitfs.com
Date: 2026-11-25T15:34:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Evaluating prepay options — ramp & auto top-ups

Thanks, team — this looks good and aligns with what Finance wanted. Orbit is willing to commit to a 36-month staged prepay with smoothed monthly releases if Redwood can provide the following:
- 18% unit discount on the 3-year total commitment (we'd need executive approval if less than that)
- auto-topup emergency pad up to 10% pre-authorized on the PO (net30)
- per-request logs retained 13 months with monthly export capability

I'll get procurement to issue an initial PO for year 1 coverage while legal finalizes the SOW. Please include the HubSpot deal id when you send the DocuSign link (HS-112233).

Best,
Susan Liu
Head of AI Platform
Orbit Financial Systems

---
Forwarded for context: procurement asked about price point sensitivity and whether a stepped discount for year 2/3 is possible — Marissa / Rishi can you propose a sliding discount schedule that preserves tail economics?
